Read file results/research/issue121/rounds/round_20261027_071611_987/agents/ideation_1/ideas.txt, lines 1-49
1: IDEA: predecessor_contrast_offset
2: TITLE: Predecessor-region contrast offset on the item latent
3: MOTIVATION: An item's own content latent should remain decisive for SID identity, while training transitions provide a directional cue about which first-level code region is useful for next-item prediction. A hard co-consumption negative supplies a local contrast rather than allowing generic popularity to dominate.
4: NOVELTY: Unlike context-decides-code mechanisms (which bottleneck distinct outcomes to the number of contexts), the contextual signal perturbs each item's own differentiable latent before the ordinary first-level nearest-code decision. Unlike an auxiliary transition loss, behaviour and curvature jointly change the actual assignment input.
5: CHANGE: Once per epoch compute fixed-curvature Poincare Frechet barycentres of current first-level codepoints for each item's observed training predecessors and its hardest eligible training co-consumption negative. Shift x_i a small, concentration-gated fraction toward the predecessor barycentre and away from the negative barycentre; select the first code by squared Euclidean distance from the shifted latent, then retain baseline residual quantisation at later levels.
6: SPECIFICATION: Freeze train-only predecessor sets P(i) and user-item sets U(i). Let n(i)=argmax_{j: J(i,j)>0, j not in P(i)} J(i,j), with deterministic item-ID tie-break, where J(i,j)=|U(i)∩U(j)|/|U(i)∪U(j)|. At each epoch compute b_i=FrechetMean_{Poincare(c=1)}{v_{a_1(j)}:j∈P(i)} and r_i analogously for n(i)'s predecessor set (empty set maps to 0). Let q_i(k) be the training predecessor mass assigned to first-level region k; gamma_i=0 if P(i) empty, else 1-H(q_i)/log(max(2,K)). Set d_i=(b_i-x_i)-0.5(r_i-x_i), z_i=x_i+w*gamma_i*d_i (w=0.1, bounded as specified below), and a_1(i)=argmin_k ||z_i-v_k||². Use z_i only for selecting a_1; baseline reconstruction and residual levels remain unchanged. Recompute barycentres after each epoch's codebook update. Distributed codebook access must use the unwrapped model/module at four-rank DDP.
7: COST: One-time training-split graph construction costs sparse user-set intersections for co-consumption candidates; cache predecessor/negative lists. Per epoch, barycentre accumulation is O(E_pred*d + N*d) plus O(N*K*d) nearest-code work already comparable to baseline; use cached predecessor-region aggregates to avoid edge-wise recomputation. At frozen scale N=24,556, 24 steps/epoch, 3,000 epochs: one barycentre refresh per epoch and 24,556 small shifts/assignments per epoch, targeting near-baseline ~0.15 s/epoch on four cards; profile because Frechet iterations may exceed budget.
8: HYPOTHESIS: Directed predecessor regions contain predictive structure beyond item content, and repelling each item from its strongest non-predecessor co-consumption neighbour reduces context-induced aliasing without collapsing item-level outcomes. Keep only if both-on improves Stage3 test Recall@10 toward/above 0.065 versus baseline and behavior-off, with no unacceptable reconstruction-loss or runtime increase.
9: RISKS: Sparse or noisy predecessor sets, unstable hard negatives, zero/near-zero entropy denominators, codebook movement making barycentres stale within an epoch, and the bounded shift still distorting reconstruction can erase gains. Jaccard candidate construction can be costly unless sparse and cached. Poincare barycentre iteration may break the epoch-time target.
10: BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed training-only predecessor relation plus training-only co-consumption Jaccard for a hard negative.
11: BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split only, add edge j→i when j is an observed immediate predecessor of i in a training sequence. For each item pair co-consumption J is the Jaccard overlap of the sets of training users interacting with each item. Select the maximum-J item not in i's observed predecessor set; freeze all lists and weights before Stage2.
12: LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: Construct user sets, transitions, candidate negatives, and predecessor-region masses exclusively from training interactions. Do not read validation/test interactions or future sequence positions. These frozen structures are the only behaviour inputs to Stage2; Stage3 validation/test is used only for the frozen evaluation protocol.
13: HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Fixed-curvature (c=1) Poincare Frechet barycentre, minimizing the sum of squared Poincare distances to the assigned codepoints.
